slides.title: Loop mode, loop seam and speed scale
slides.source: Source: Chapter 10, “Frames, sprite sheets and cycles”; glossary, Animation foundations; Godot AnimationPlayer class reference (speed_scale).
slides.notes: Speed scale: time to finish = length divided by speed_scale. Walk-cycle values are illustrative.
slides.picture: Playhead position over six seconds for three loop modes; two loops with and without a seam jump; three speed scales racing a clip.

new_texts: Whether a clip plays once, loops or ping-pongs.
PLAYHEAD POSITION OVER 6 S, CLIP LENGTH 2 S
Loop mode: play once, loop, or ping-pong. At 6 s a 2 s clip is stopped, back at 0, or at its end.
all_texts: Whether a clip plays once, loops or ping-pongs.
PLAYHEAD POSITION OVER 6 S, CLIP LENGTH 2 S
Loop mode: play once, loop, or ping-pong. At 6 s a 2 s clip is stopped, back at 0, or at its end.

new_texts: A jump where the last value meets the first on a loop. Test that they match.
TWO LOOPS OF A WALK-CYCLE ANGLE
A loop seam is the jump when the last value meets the first. Compare the value at 0 and at length.
all_texts: Whether a clip plays once, loops or ping-pongs.

new_texts: A multiplier on how fast a clip plays. 0.5 is half speed.

Speed scale divides the time. Half speed takes twice as long; double speed takes half.

slides.title: Before you trust an animation change
slides.picture: A checklist of six items drawn one at a time.

new_texts: Does a designer need to scrub it? Then an Animation. Gameplay sets the end value? A Tween.
If it loops, do the first and last values match, and is the loop mode set?
Is a yes-or-no property keyed with update mode discrete?
